observations: Orange gas cylinder with a brass valve and a handle.
The cylinder has visible surface wear, scratches, and some paint loss on the body.
A label is present on the side, but the text is too blurry to read in the provided photos.
The cylinder is shown in a storage or shop environment with other gas cylinders and equipment in the background.
The seller claims the cylinder is 'Recently tested and certified, no leak, the valve is new.'

claims.evidence: The weight is not legible in the photos.

claims.claim: Recently tested and certified, no leak, the valve is new.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The cylinder may be expired or past its re-qualification date.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacture and expiry dates stamped on the cylinder.

risks.risk: The cylinder may have been used for illegal or hazardous purposes.
risks.proof: A photo of the cylinder with a clear view of the stamped capacity and the date stamp.

risks.risk: The valve may be leaking or not sealing properly.
risks.proof: A video showing a soap bubble test on the valve threads.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Clear photo of the stamped date and expiry on the cylinder.
Video of a leak test on the valve.
Photo of the cylinder with the handle and valve fully visible.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
